name: Refugee Status (UNHCR Mandate Determination, No Domestic Legal Status)

requirements.blocker_text: Cuba is not a signatory to the international refugee conventions and has no domestic legal framework or national mechanism for determining refugee status -- per legal expert Eloy Viera Canive, quoted in independent Cuban press, 'the main problem is that in Cuba refugee status does not legally exist.' UNHCR operates as the sole authority determining who qualifies, coordinating informally with Cuba's Foreign Ministry, entirely outside Cuban law. Recognized refugees can access some UNHCR-facilitated services (education for an estimated ~89 young refugees, food assistance, economic aid for housing) but hold NO Cuban legal status: authorities may expel a foreigner if their conduct is deemed contrary to state interests, with no appeal process, and reportedly nearly half of asylum seekers in Cuba lack any legal status at all -- making resettlement to a third country the primary long-term outcome for most.
requirements.fix_path: Contact UNHCR to register -- there is no Cuban government office or legal process to apply to, and recognition carries no guaranteed protection from expulsion.

outcome.duration_length: precarious; no fixed legal duration since no Cuban legal status exists

sources.title: elTOQUE (independent Cuban press) -- confirms Cuba is not a signatory to international refugee conventions and has no domestic legal framework; UNHCR operates entirely outside Cuban law; arbitrary-expulsion risk with no appeal

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Cuba). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to independent Cuban journalism, tier 4; UNHCR's own Cuba help portal was reached but its specific rights page returned a 404, and Cuba's government domains were systematically unreachable in this build. MARQUEE STRUCTURAL FINDING, the most severe humanitarian-protection gap documented in this dataset so far: unlike Algeria and Haiti (both built earlier), where UNHCR at least conducts mandate-based determination in a comparatively stable operating environment, Cuba's own reporting describes recognized refugees facing ARBITRARY EXPULSION with NO APPEAL PROCESS, and nearly half of asylum seekers holding no legal status of any kind -- a materially harsher practical reality than the 'no domestic law but functioning UNHCR process' pattern seen elsewhere. All outcome fields are modeled at their most restrictive/conservative setting to reflect this, per the source's own explicit description rather than an assumption.
